purpose: Complete published baseline reproduction, then the frozen 25% BITLSTM blend selected from fixture and package comparisons. No full enwik9 result has been measured.
procedure: Pin encoder and decoder to one logical CPU. First run the published baseline and require its complete archive hash, exact isolated SFX restoration and resource record. Then run the frozen blend on the same host with the same input and procedure. Preserve all outcomes including failure or regression; compare total packaged bytes only after both pass.
scoring: compressor bytes + actual completed SFX archive bytes + 19 bytes for comp9.args. Do not infer a candidate score before completing compression and exact restoration.
limitations: Sampling can miss short resource peaks and is not a hard memory/disk cap. The 10 GiB RSS stop threshold follows upstream operational units; record raw bytes and use judging rules for eligibility.

Scratch sampling counts regular files in the active working directory and open file descriptors of the process tree, including unnamed/deleted temporary files. It is not a complete audit of all filesystem activity.
The separate decoder directory is not a filesystem or network sandbox; no claim of enforced self-containment follows from that alone.
Pinned CPU affinity does not reserve or isolate a physical core from other jobs. Record idle-host conditions and a measured Geekbench 5 score before assessing normalized runtime.
The 240000-second timeout is an operational bound, not the prize time allowance. Each phase needs independent machine-normalized evaluation.
Hosted six-hour CI cannot run this protocol to completion. A persistent native Linux host remains required; none is currently configured.

candidate_model.kind: 25% blend of two one-pass BITLSTM checkpoints
